title: The control is only as good as the handoff
mainJudgement: The control is only as good as the handoff.

committeeQuestion.question: When an alert lands outside the normal operating day, who can assess it, intervene and show why the decision was made?
committeeQuestion.why: The SEC's 24-hour-market agenda and Anthropic's new enterprise safeguards make the same practical point: a control needs a named recipient, real authority and an evidence trail when the usual team is not in the room.
committeeQuestion.evidence: One recent out-of-hours alert, its time-stamped triage and escalation record, intervention authority, decision maker, customer or market-impact assessment, remediation action and closure evidence.

committeeQuestions.question: For a high-value payment that looks wrong, how quickly can the firm stop it, contact the customer and record the decision?
committeeQuestions.why: The Central Bank of Ireland reports that payment-fraud value rose 27.2% in 2025, with authorised push-payment fraud and cross-border transfers carrying a growing share of loss. Detection is only useful if the intervention route works in time.
committeeQuestions.evidence: The fraud scenario, alert thresholds, hold or release authority, contact path, decision record, recovery outcome and a recent test of the customer-support handoff.

committeeQuestions.question: Can the firm reconstruct one cyber or AI-related alert from the original event to closure without relying on someone’s memory?
committeeQuestions.why: CISA's exploited-vulnerability update and AWS's CloudTrail investigation guidance point to the same discipline: asset ownership, logs, exception decisions and proof of remediation must still be available after the technical work is done.
committeeQuestions.evidence: The original alert, relevant logs, named system owner, vulnerability or model decision, accepted exception if any, remediation evidence, independent retest and dated closure record.

judgement.observation: Anthropic's new safeguards put AI activity logs under customer control. The CFTC changed clearing requirements for certain CAD and MXN swaps. Ireland's central bank reports payment-fraud losses up 27%, and CISA has added another exploited vulnerability.
judgement.executiveJudgement: These are all handoff problems: who receives a signal, who can act, and can the firm later show what happened? That is where an otherwise sound process often thins out—overnight, across teams, or when a payment or incident needs a decision now.
judgement.implication: Choose one control that cannot wait for office hours. Follow a recent alert through detection, decision, intervention and closure. If the owner, permission or record is vague, fix it.
